questions.stem: A geocoding vendor's contract allows 50 requests per second. The client puts each call behind a `new Semaphore(50)`, with acquire() before the call and release() in a finally after it. Calls take about 20 ms, and 200 request threads are busy geocoding. Roughly what does the vendor receive?

options.text: About 2,500 requests a second, since each permit is taken again as soon as its call ends
options.says: permits bound how many calls run at once; a 20 ms call frees its permit 50 times a second, so 50 permits carry about 2,500 calls

options.text: About 50 requests a second, since each permit is taken again only once a second has passed
options.says: a permit comes back when release() is called, at the end of the call; a semaphore has no clock

options.text: About 200 requests a second, since each busy thread holds one permit in turn
options.says: only 50 threads hold permits at a time, and each one finishes 50 calls a second

options.text: About 200 requests a second, since each waiting thread is let in once per release cycle
options.says: there is no release cycle; every release lets one waiter in at once, so the rate follows the call time

origin.section: A Semaphore Counts Permits: It Limits How Many Threads Are Inside, Not Which Ones

questions.stem: A settings store guards its state with `Semaphore mutex = new Semaphore(1)`. save() calls mutex.acquire(), writes the settings, and then calls audit(), which also calls mutex.acquire() before appending to the audit log; each method releases in its own finally. One thread calls save(), with no other thread using the store. What happens?

options.text: save() never returns, since audit() waits for a permit that only its own thread holds
options.says: a semaphore is not reentrant: the second acquire needs a second permit, and the only one is held by the same thread, which is now waiting

options.text: save() never returns, since audit() waits for a permit that only another thread may release
options.says: any thread may release a permit, the holder included; the holder can't because it is the thread that waits

options.text: save() returns normally, since the thread holding the permit may take it again
options.says: that is the hold count of a ReentrantLock; a semaphore keeps only a count and does not know who took the permit

options.text: save() returns normally, since audit() is handed the permit save() still holds
options.says: a permit is not handed between methods; audit()'s acquire() needs a free permit and there is none

origin.section: A Semaphore Has No Owner and Trusts Every Release: Release Exactly What You Acquired

questions.stem: An API gateway forwards requests to a backend that accepts 20 at once: `try { if (!slots.tryAcquire(100, MILLISECONDS)) return busy(); return forward(request); } finally { slots.release(); }`, with `slots = new Semaphore(20)`. During a spike, 300 requests get busy(). Once the spike is over, how many requests can the gateway forward at the same time?

options.text: Up to 320, since every busy() return still ran the finally and added a permit
options.says: release() checks nothing; every refused request added a permit it never took, so the count grew by 300

options.text: Up to 20, since the finally added a permit only on the returns that had taken one
options.says: the finally runs on every path out of the try, the return of busy() included, and release() adds a permit each time

options.text: Up to 20, since release() refused the permits from threads that had taken none
options.says: a semaphore has no owner; release() adds a permit whoever calls it

options.text: Up to 320 for the next 300 calls, since each extra permit is dropped once it is used
options.says: a permit is not marked extra; once added it stays in the count for good, and every call returns it

origin.section: A Semaphore Has No Owner and Trusts Every Release: Release Exactly What You Acquired

questions.stem: A print service shares two printers through `new Semaphore(2, true)`. Print jobs call acquire(). A health probe calls tryAcquire() every second and, when it gets a permit, releases it at once. Both printers are busy and three jobs are queued when one printer finishes, just as the probe runs. Who can get that printer?

options.text: The probe can get it ahead of the first queued job, since tryAcquire() takes a permit that is free at that moment
options.says: the untimed tryAcquire() barges even on a fair semaphore; tryAcquire(0, SECONDS) would respect the queue

options.text: The probe can get it ahead of the first queued job, since a fair semaphore orders only acquire() calls made after it was created
options.says: the order covers every queued acquire; the probe gets ahead because tryAcquire() ignores the queue

options.text: Only the first queued job can get it, since tryAcquire() on a fair semaphore refuses while threads are queued
options.says: that is what tryAcquire(0, SECONDS) does; the untimed tryAcquire() takes a free permit regardless

options.text: Only the first queued job can get it, since release() hands the permit straight to the head of the queue
options.says: release() adds a permit and wakes a waiter; a tryAcquire() made before the waiter runs can take it

origin.section: When the Permits Run Out, Choose: Wait, Wait a Bounded Time, or Refuse
